Time noise is about ±0.03 s.

Mechanisms I believe:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with total optimizer steps, at about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Every time cut (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037) bought time at a roughly dial-like rate, with no free lunch except the systems levers.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Backward truncation of the stem saves more time than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze lost about 0.4 pp. E042's partial freeze was neutral within noise.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a narrow local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by about −0.1 pp.
5. Systems-only math-identical work gives about 1–2% each. It keeps per-seed outcomes bit-identical (E035), but E043 shows reruns can drift, so bit-reproducibility is imperfect.
6. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw.
7. Sample dropping (E031) costs about 0.3 pp for about 0.6 s, which is no better than the epoch dial.

4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a narrow local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by about −0.1 pp.

forecasts.reason: Group-2 backward is about half of the MACs but only 10% of steps are affected, so it saves about 0.1 s. Accuracy cost is likely 0.1–0.2 pp, since group 2 is still learning late.
Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the numbers should match the tip within noise. The profile will probably show conv1 with low efficiency and memory-bound kernels on the 31×31 maps.
Dropping 5% of samples cuts about 11 steps, which saves about 0.15 s. The accuracy cost is about 0.1–0.15 pp, which is about the dial rate and within noise.
The math is identical, so accuracy should hold, although rebuilt graphs can drift. Aligning Cin to 32 probably saves 1–3% of time if conv1 is inefficient.

cruxes: Does the profile show that group-1 conv1 (Cin=24) is inefficient? If it does, channel padding is a free 2–4% of time.
What is the true unselected population mean of the tip? If it is below 0.752, no further time cuts are affordable.
Does the late-freeze nonlinearity extend to group 2, or is the 75% freeze point specific to group 1?
